It should be a web app with great design. ===== THIS PHASE'S DISCUSSION SO FAR ===== (You are the first speaker.) ===== PHASE PLAYBOOK (editable phase_rules.json) ===== Global app-build rules: - Prefer a smaller finished app over a larger half-built app. - Every generated app must have real user-visible behavior, not only placeholder screens. - For iOS apps, default to SwiftUI, deterministic local state first, Apple system frameworks, and no third-party package unless it materially reduces risk. - Every screen needs empty, loading, success, and error states when the workflow can reach those states. - No two text or control elements may visually overlap, collide, or clip each other. Labels never sit on top of values; values never stack into each other. When elements are positioned by a data value (times on a timeline, points on an axis), enforce a minimum gap and de-clutter (offset, group, collapse, or drop a colliding label) — overlapping text is a broken screen. - The interface must never claim an outcome that has not happened: show Saved/Deleted/Sent/Synced/Unlocked only after it is truly confirmed, never a success state shown unconditionally. No sample or placeholder data shown as if it were the user's real data. - Implement the design spec's tokens as one SwiftUI theme file (e.g. Theme.swift with type, spacing, and color definitions) and reference it everywhere; never scatter font/size/color literals through views. - Every generated app must fully support dark mode: semantic color roles with explicit light and dark values, verified in both appearances. - Empty states are designed content (icon + one-line explanation + the action that fills the screen), never a blank view or bare 'No data' text. - No default unstyled List, Form, or navigation chrome where the design spec calls for custom rows, cards, or backgrounds; the built UI must match the spec. - Treat accessibility, privacy, persistence, and testing as product requirements, not polish. - Do not declare the app done until build verification and the final review agree on what works and what remains limited. Phase rules: - Preserve the user's original prompt before interpreting it. - Convert the prompt into hard requirements, non-goals, output shape, quality bar, and decision rules. - Resolve conflicts by naming the assumption, not by silently changing the assignment. Required output: - Original prompt excerpt or full prompt reference. - Hard requirements. - Non-goals. - Production-readiness definition. - Decision rules for later phases. - A NUMBERED list of testable requirements extracted from the user's prompt — each one verifiable by using the app. Acceptance checks before consensus: - A later phase can tell whether it is violating the user's prompt. - Multi-app quantity/category requirements are explicit. - Production-ready means more than a prototype or spec. - Every promise in the original prompt maps to a numbered requirement; nothing is silently dropped. ===== RELEVANT KNOWLEDGE (curated WEB reference — use it, don't restate it) ===== ----- Web Ui Styling A11Y ----- # Web UI: Structure, Styling, Responsive Layout, Design Tokens & Accessibility Dense reference for building correct, accessible, maintainable web UI in 2026. Examples use React/JSX + TypeScript, but the rules generalize. Every snippet is idiomatic and compiles. --- ## Component Structure ### Rules - **One component, one responsibility.** If a component both fetches data and renders complex layout, split it (container/presentational, or hook + view). - **Colocate** the component, its styles, tests, and stories in one folder: `Button/{Button.tsx, Button.module.css, Button.test.tsx}`. - **Props over prop-drilling.** Reach for context only for cross-cutting concerns (theme, auth, locale, router), not to avoid passing 2 props. - **Composition over boolean explosion.** Don't accumulate `isPrimary`, `isLarge`, `hasIcon`. Use `variant`/`size` union types and slot children. - **Controlled where the parent needs the value; uncontrolled otherwise.** Don't mirror props into state — derive during render. - **Render the correct element.** A thing that navigates is ``; a thing that acts is `
